thread:
maya: Heads up — customers reporting 502s on payments-prod, but our incident gateway didn't page the oncall. Not seeing a page in the last 10m.Anyone else seeing alerts?

oncall-bot: automated: alert received: payments-prod/checkout-5xx (severity: P1) — decision: NO PAGE (suppression match: route=payments, policy=quiet-hours) :warning:

sara: Wait — quiet-hours should NOT suppress payments-prod. That policy was supposed to exempt billing routes after the policy change last week.

lee: I can confirm alerts hit the gateway at 02:18 UTC — logs show 200 OK to /webhook but response body was empty. grabbing logs now.

maya: @sara @lee if the gateway erroneously matched a suppression rule we need live mitigation. Are customers impacted?

lee: partial impact — some requests got 502s, Mobile app retries show increased latency and a few checkout failures. CS already triaged a spike in support tickets.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook suggestion: 1) manually page current oncall 2) disable suppression matcher 3) revert last suppression policy change 4) rotate webhook signing key if mismatch suspected

maya: I'm manually paging the rotation-oncall now. @oncall-bot please force page to schedule:rotation-oncall (override reason: missed automation)

oncall-bot: automated: forced page sent to @lee (rotation-oncall). Incident channel created: #inc-1778501234-payments-502

lee: got the page, I'm on it. Quick check: suppression matcher returned true because the gateway parsed header `x-service` as `internal` — but the header is `payments` in our preprod tests. looks like header parsing regex changed in the deploy at 02:15.

maya: rollback window? Who rolled at 02:15?

sara: I pushed a small rule to incident-gateway to normalize service header (PR #842). That change was supposed to be safe — sounds like it inverted the regex for certain headers. rolling back now.

lee: rolling back confirmed — incident bot now shows a new decision: PAGE. Re-sending page to rotation-oncall.

oncall-bot: automated: alert evaluated: payments-prod/checkout-5xx — decision: PAGE, routed to schedule:rotation-oncall. Paging attempt 1 sent.

ops-runbook-bot: note: investigate how suppression policy unit tests missed this case — add test for header variants and a canary in staging before gateway rule changes.

maya: Good catch. Customer impact: we have ~0.6% failed checkouts last 15m, CS says ~120 tickets. Need an RCA thread after stabilization. For now, are we confident rollback fixes both paging and 502s?

lee: rollback fixed paging decision. For 502s we see immediate drop in errors after rollback — looks like the changed header normalization also affected upstream routing to payment-service instances. Still watching metrics.

maya: OK — continue monitoring. I'll notify support leadership and draft a short status update for customers. Assigning @sara to own the follow-up remediation (tests + canary) and @lee to validate monitoring dashboards and paging rules.

sara: on it — will open a follow-up PR with tests and staging canary steps.

lee: monitoring shows error rate back to baseline at +6m post-rollback. closing live mitigation, leaving incident open for RCA. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks everyone. Quick retro action: add an alert on incident-gateway policy-change deploys that are not followed by an automated canary validation. Also update runbook step to include immediate manual page if decision flips from NO PAGE -> PAGE within 10m.

ops-runbook-bot: action items recorded: "add canary for gateway policy changes", "add policy-change alert", "add unit tests for header parsing".

maya: I'll schedule a 30m post-incident sync in #eng-sre in 1h.

lee: filing timeline notes in the incident channel now.

sara: filing PR link and tests in the incident thread when ready.

oncall-bot: automated: incident channel #inc-1778501234-payments-502 archived after idle 30m (manual close may be needed).
